combat2_operational_work.evidence: The source-of-truth matrix is recorded in docs/design/combat2-targeting-initiation-audit.md. Selection is local-only; Basic Attack engagement is transactional; queued manual targets remain frozen; captured refused intents consume the slot; autoattack retargets by server ordering; peaceful observers do not qualify for rewards. Proven gaps: movement does not invoke combat entry, party follower entry can depend on each browser, arbitrary hostile first-action engagement has no RPC, and installed tank ordering retains designated-party priority. These coupled gaps remain ENG-COMBAT-002. Independent spendable-CP client and RPC preflight corrections are authored. ENG-MOVE-001 and heartbeat identity/cutoff work are unchanged.

Static installed-contract tracing proves one lifecycle defect: settle_out_of_combat_resources considered e.claim_token independently of f.present, so a historical absent fighter could remain excluded when its reactivated encounter generation held a live claim. Resolver completion, commit status persistence, claim clearing, the enabled inactive-fighter release trigger and client detachment otherwise form the intended sequence. The forward migration scopes both living-opposition and live-claim ownership to present fighters. Executable transition tests cover final combat interval exclusion, next-boundary HP/CP/MP settlement without banking, aggressive and deliberately peaceful completion, multiple survivors, a dead member, live and expired claims, duplicate settlement and immediate re-entry. No Cloud access was available, so the exact predicate present on Mik's most recent live row remains unobserved and post-combat regeneration remains unverified.

Root causes were client delivery and presentation boundaries, not evidence of a changed server cadence. Character rows had scoped Realtime but no connection-state diagnostics or bounded visible-tab fallback, so tab focus could appear to be required when Realtime delivery stalled. Combat2 visible history was encounter-keyed and could be replaced or cleared at release, while the on-device archive received the legacy local log instead of the merged authoritative presentation. The correction retains scoped Realtime as primary, adds a coalesced four-second visible fallback and recovery refreshes, fences stale user responses, refreshes resources when an active Combat2 session exits, retains a bounded 100-event character-scoped log across release/movement/new encounters, and archives that merged view. The overlay no longer presents a stale cursor as an encounter tick outside combat. Operator-observed roughly eight-second UI updates are presentation evidence only; without timestamped Cloud rows they do not prove server settlement cadence. No Cloud, SQL, scheduler, resolver, Edge or gameplay mutation occurred.

Authoritative out-of-combat HP/CP/MP settlement is installed and composed into the existing world scheduler: one four-second logical interval, globally locked singleton cursor, already_settled short-circuit, short catch-up capped at three intervals, at most one interval after longer downtime, cursor advanced without banking while the world sleeps, combat mode is closed or the dispatcher schedule is absent. Settlement and Combat2 dispatch failures are independently contained with sanitized SQLSTATE evidence and the aggregate result is ok only when both domains succeed. Exclusions: death or missing location, Test Arena node, queued or just-resolved solo departure, queued or just-resolved party departure membership, fresh respawn request, fresh fighter release, and active-encounter ownership (present fighter with a living engaged creature in that same encounter, or a live claim). Peaceful co-location, inert shells, absent fighters and ended encounters do not suppress settlement. Formulas use final effective attributes from valid equipped durable gear and gems: HP from effective CON plus gear HP, gear regen, milestone and Inn bonuses; CP from effective WIS plus milestone and Inn; MP from effective DEX plus Inn. Caps are enforced, an already higher value is never lowered, browser-local food contributes nothing, Combat2 CP regeneration and Inspire are untouched and the browser has no resource writer or settlement privilege. Live regeneration is not yet verified; no settlement, dispatcher, worker, movement, combat, party or arena call was made.

Root cause proven in client presentation source, not in the database. GamePage restricted the visible node roster to creatures contained in the authoritative encounter presentation (creatures.filter(c => activeCombat2Presentation?.creatures.some(...))) whenever Combat2 owned the session. After the engagement/release lifecycle release, peaceful co-location no longer enters an encounter, so that filter produced an empty 'In the area' list while the minimap kept deriving presence from the node roster. Correction is frontend-only and minimal: the node roster is now the single source of creature visibility and the encounter model may only refine hp/max hp/alive for creatures it contains. No creature was marked engaged, no encounter fabricated, automatic peaceful entry was not re-enabled and selected-target fencing and late-response handling are unchanged. Guarded by src/features/combat2/creature-visibility.test.ts (5 tests) plus the existing presentation suite.

Read-only boundary evidence for the reported stall. Last successful boundary: claim. First failing boundary: commit transport. cron.job_run_details shows 2017 successful runs of public.combat2_dispatch_scheduler_fire() at the intended 2s cadence from 06:52Z until 08:00:56Z, when the world went asleep (world_state.changed_at 08:00:58Z), so world wake, scheduler and dispatcher were all healthy and the node was selected by due-node discovery. The active encounter at the reported node held a present fighter and one living engaged creature and its claim was refreshed every 2 seconds (claimed tick 5 above committed tick 4), proving claim, decode and resolve succeeded repeatedly. Every dispatch attempt then returned commit_transport_error with PostgreSQL-category SQLSTATE 42703 (undefined column) at the commit stage. node_tick_commit and both installed wrappers trap all errors and return internal_failure, so a 42703 surfacing as a transport failure originates outside the PL/pgSQL body (PostgREST/pooler request handling or post-return deferred work). Ability submission did not bypass anything: it changed proposal content, so the failure is proposal-content dependent rather than input driven. Deferred-trigger candidates were inspected and release_stances_on_death is excluded (it returns before planning any statement while hp > 0). Postgres error logs for the window are no longer retained and no diagnostic recording covered it, so the exact undefined column remains unproven. Proving it requires one separately authorized bounded probe of node_tick_commit; no such invocation was performed and no gameplay row was repaired. ROOT CAUSE PROVEN 2026-09-23 (static catalog audit, no encounter touched): the missing column is character_inventory.status (equally node_ground_loot.status), referenced as NEW.status by the installed trigger function public.enforce_unique_holder_identity(), authored in migration 20260917133413_fc7e672e-18b4-4103-9e8a-40f493fa167f.sql line 99. Installed body matched repository source byte-for-byte, so this is an authored source defect and not installed drift. The function is attached to three tables of different shape (character_inventory, node_ground_loot, marketplace_listings) as DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED constraint triggers; only marketplace_listings has a status column. PL/pgSQL resolves record field references when it prepares the entire IF expression, so "TG_TABLE_NAME='marketplace_listings' AND NEW.status<>'active' AND ..." raises SQLSTATE 42703 (record "new" has no field "status") on EVERY write to the other two tables regardless of the TG_TABLE_NAME guard. Because the trigger is deferred it fires at COMMIT, after node_tick_commit has returned, so the error escapes both wrappers' EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS handlers and reaches the worker as an unclassifiable commit transport failure. Failing branch: any proposal whose commit writes character_inventory, i.e. any tick recording weapon durability wear; proposals with no inventory write were unaffected, which is why an ability cast appeared correlated with progress. Static tests did not catch it because they assert column existence and authored SQL text, never PL/pgSQL record-field resolution against the installed table shape; the new guard closes that gap. Semantics confirmed in one single-connection transaction using only ON COMMIT DROP temp objects and a pg_temp clone, rolled back: the old expression raised 42703 at SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE, the corrected expression passed. No gameplay table was read for mutation, no public function was replaced in the probe, and all protected fingerprints (character_inventory durability, node_encounter tick/claim/state_version/status, characters hp/cp/max_cp/mp/reserved_buffs, node_creature hp/alive, node_intent, node_pending_event, node_tick_log) are byte-identical before and after. CORRECTION: forward migration 20260923084603_63ed1235-60fa-4f63-a4a6-f37673d50ae8.sql (sha256 4f30b604887f6d24e04dfc3d6cf24adfbc4a4f9676bef21076d28982872b60d4) replaces the function body only: the marketplace-only column is now read as to_jsonb(NEW)->>'status' inside the TG_TABLE_NAME branch, which resolves at runtime and is valid on every attached table. All three identity rules, the three deferred triggers, deterministic resolution, claim/commit fencing, exactly-once ticks, scheduler cadence, lease duration, WIS CP regeneration, engagement/release lifecycle, peaceful-creature visibility, movement, departures, rewards and ADM-025B are unchanged. Fail-closed assertions in the migration verify the installed body no longer references NEW.status, that character_inventory still has no status column, that marketplace_listings still has one, and that the three deferred triggers exist and are enabled. Security linter count unchanged (323, no new findings). No schema shape change, so official types were not regenerated; the Combat2 edge mirror regenerated with no diff, so no Edge Function required deployment and none was invoked. product_backlog.evidence: Product request recorded, not designed or implemented. After a character has been logged out/inactive for a configured period, reset its authoritative position to the default city/start location. The period should preferably reference the same configured duration already used for unique-item inactivity/loss rather than duplicating a hard-coded number. The initial destination is the current default city/start node, described by the operator as position 0,0; before implementation it must be verified whether 0,0 is an authoritative coordinate, a map-presentation concept or shorthand for a specific node id. Future extension: let a character choose an authoritative personal home/bind/start location. The reset must never occur while the character holds a live combat claim, participates in an active encounter, has a queued movement or departure, an active marketplace or other protected transaction, or any other incompatible lifecycle state. 'Logged out/inactive' must be defined from authoritative session/activity evidence, not browser presence. Idempotency and safe interaction with parties and followers must be resolved before implementation. No schema, RPC, timer or cleanup job was added.
